text:
The fault is most likely in **M5**. Its NMOS pull-up has its gate on `ibias` (≈0.78 V) and its source on `vout`, so it behaves as a source follower. Its Vgs is 0.699 V, below its 0.77 V threshold, so it sits in subthreshold and can deliver only about 2.3 µA. Because the pull-up cannot lift `vout` above roughly `ibias − Vth(M5)` ≈ 0.01–0.1 V, `vout` settles at 0.084 V. M6 is then pushed into triode, which is consistent with its reported operating point.

The low DC level propagates to the input. Through Rf, `iin` also sits at 0.084 V, below M1's 0.625 V threshold, so M1 is off and the first-stage loop gain collapses. That explains the 83.5 dBΩ transimpedance (versus about 113 dBΩ from Rf alone), the poor f3dB, and the high input-referred noise. M2 showing zero current is a consequence of M1 being off, not a separate fault.

This pins vout low, pushes M6 into triode, drops iin below M1's threshold so M1/M2 carry no current, and collapses the loop gain (zt, f3db, noise). Restore the intended pull-up (gate drive/size or device type) so vout settles in 0.3-1.5 V and M1 is biased."}
